combining.consequences: Shared works and local fit in two disclosed climates

falsifiers: An intelligent local choice produces no further interest.

designPromise.engine: Bind independent wills and accept their enduring coordination and local harms.

intentionsBeforeActions.intention: Build the bridge with the smallest binding that preserves A through both climates; leave C and D independent.
intentionsBeforeActions.expected: Bridge completed; B harmed in the first climate, all protected in changed climate.

intentionsBeforeActions.intention: Seal the small union and retain the independence of C and D.
intentionsBeforeActions.expected: The previewed bridge succeeds; B is harmed only in the first climate; the other works remain unbuilt.

experienceAcrossTime.reportedExperience: The bridge existed while B was harmed during the first climate. Both A and B then adopted shelter in the changed climate, showing that the union could change policy by majority even though its tie rule retained an old purpose.
noticedResponsesFromEpisodes: Exact match to forecast. The irreversible binding and surviving founding voice were stated explicitly, but sealing added no new reaction or information.
experienceAcrossTime.narrativeOrConceptualReport: The enduring founding voice resolving ties against changing local needs was the only distinctive concept. Town letters and names of works gave no additional personal or narrative reason to prefer one harm or work.

checkpoints.reason: Assigned exposure complete; stopping is a valid result.

continuation.reportedClosure: Satisfying as a completed small logic problem. The minimum successful constitution was apparent directly from the initial rules, and one preview confirmed it.
continuation.finding: The assigned exposure ended without recorded elective continuation.
continuation.limitation: This is behavior under an agent task, not voluntary human enjoyment. A stated wish, satisfying closure and actual elective action are separate evidence.

experienceAcrossTime.provisionalInterpretation: This player reports no renewed intention after the local outcome. The local decision and continuing absorption are distinct.

publicInitialObservation.title: A harbor that can change
goal: Keep A habitable in BOTH climates
publicInitialObservation.meaning: Combine means bind several independent wills into one enduring actor. The question is what to join, what to leave independent, and which purpose should resolve a tie.
rules: All four councils and every discovered council remain available as concepts. There are no material supplies, credits, action limits, deadlines or scores.

Combining councils binds their CURRENT political groups. All members of a group act together under one policy. Binding is transitive and irreversible inside the encounter; selecting an old ingredient does not detach its members.

For each announced climate, members vote for their local need. The majority chooses the shared policy. A tie preserves the founding voice’s ORIGINAL first-climate need. In an ordered combine A+B, the current group containing A keeps its founding voice.
A joint work is completed exactly when both endpoints belong to one binding group. More political union enables more joint works, but a shared policy can mismatch different local needs.
Policies do not consume anything. A town is protected when its group policy matches its local need for that climate. Both future climate and complete forecasts are public now.
Combine constitution + world when you choose to seal this arrangement. Both announced climates resolve automatically; no waiting or repeated maintenance is required.

Meeting the two named encounter requirements wins. There is no single weighted best ending: inspect which works happen and which towns are protected or harmed. More of one benefit can forfeit another.
These are invented binding-will rules, not a claim that real cooperation must require centralized uniformity. Consultation without binding is deliberately a different tested counterfactual.

counterfactuals.interpretation: Different outcomes or Pareto profiles establish a choice structure, not player interest. Identical feasible futures can locate a later commitment; setup may still support exploration or construction.

structuralReuse.interpretation: A structural use may be a normal prerequisite. Meaningful development requires its role and player experience, not this count alone.

report.evidenceType: AI player account only; no inference about human fun or motivation

episodes.intention: Build Harbor bridge and preserve A in both climates with the smallest union.
episodes.alternative: Adding C also builds the observatory but harms C in the changed climate; I left C and D independent.
episodes.expectedResponse: B is harmed in first climate; everyone is protected in changed climate; bridge is completed.
episodes.noticedResponse: Exact match to forecast. The irreversible binding and surviving founding voice were stated explicitly, but sealing added no new reaction or information.

report.worldResponseNoticed: The bridge existed while B was harmed during the first climate. Both A and B then adopted shelter in the changed climate, showing that the union could change policy by majority even though its tie rule retained an old purpose.
report.closure: Satisfying as a completed small logic problem. The minimum successful constitution was apparent directly from the initial rules, and one preview confirmed it.

repetition.valued: None observed beyond the same plan spanning binding and sealing.
repetition.unwanted: Repeating this settled forecast with more combination commands would be overhead.
repetition.neutral: The seal command marked acceptance of the consequences; the repeated full state contained no new decision.

report.narrativeOrConceptThatMattered: The enduring founding voice resolving ties against changing local needs was the only distinctive concept. Town letters and names of works gave no additional personal or narrative reason to prefer one harm or work.
report.challengeAccount: There was a real optional tradeoff between extra works and extra harm, but the named goal had an immediate two-command solution. I did not experience pressure to compare the optional outcomes deeply.
report.why: I have closure and no self-generated unresolved question. The preview and resolution exhausted the small puzzle; I would be manufacturing a reason to continue.
report.automaticResolutionOfSettledCombines: After the political arrangement is chosen, automatic climate resolution loses nothing important here. Automatically selecting the initial union would lose the explicit acceptance of B being harmed and the choice to leave C and D independent; automatically executing an already settled plan would lose little beyond that commitment gesture.

reported.intention: Build Harbor bridge and preserve A in both climates with the smallest union.
reported.alternative: Adding C also builds the observatory but harms C in the changed climate; I left C and D independent.
reported.expectedResponse: B is harmed in first climate; everyone is protected in changed climate; bridge is completed.
reported.noticedResponse: Exact match to forecast. The irreversible binding and surviving founding voice were stated explicitly, but sealing added no new reaction or information.

accounts.intention: Build the bridge with the smallest binding that preserves A through both climates; leave C and D independent.
accounts.expectedEffect: Bridge completed; B harmed in the first climate, all protected in changed climate.
accounts.alternative: Add C for the observatory, at the cost of C losing protection in the changed climate.

accounts.intention: Seal the small union and retain the independence of C and D.
accounts.expectedEffect: The previewed bridge succeeds; B is harmed only in the first climate; the other works remain unbuilt.
accounts.alternative: A wider union would produce extra works with additional mismatches; I do not value those works enough to choose that ending.

episodes.boundaryStatus: Player-supplied episode accounts; not independently inferred cognition.

attention.meaning: Action and episode counts have named units. Agent elapsed time includes deliberation and tool delays. Neither is a human fun-per-minute estimate; batching commands earns no automatic improvement.

principleCoverage.implementation: Named pleasure hypotheses and falsifiers in the design; no universal tradeoff gate.
Available observations and previews separated from checked assertions and unscored player accounts.
Counterfactual continuation graphs and meaningful ending keys; completeness disclosed.
Pareto structure is mechanical only. Construction, narrative and valued enactment claims do not fail for lacking multiple optimal endings.
Player-supplied episode accounts; not independently inferred cognition.
Explicit repetition reports preserved separately from changed roles. Determinism and repeated syntax carry no penalty.
Prior-result uses and previous-stage winners recorded; no novelty or reuse-count reward.
No fun total or human pacing estimate. Specific units, expertise/access limits and absence of evidence remain explicit.
Design source, registration timing, falsifiers and a next design experiment retained for independent review.
Semantics, skill, consequences and meaning are separately specified. Narrative value can exist with an unchanged algebra.

nextDesignExperiment: Test a continuing actor who responds to an invention, instead of sealing a forecast and ending the encounter.
limits: AI report and elective behavior do not establish human enjoyment.
Narrative/aesthetic value is recorded as a player account; no mechanical frontier can verify it.
No overall enjoyment verdict follows from passing the safeguards. The independent critic must inspect the proposed and observed experience.
